Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the middle of Nova Health's procurement security review and have a few focused asks about how Redwood handles PII in inference flows before we finalize our vendor risk score. The SSQ we attached to the RFP has a couple of open items around:

- data classification used to mark PII vs non-PII across ingest and model outputs (we need concrete examples)
- cross-border transfer controls for embeddings and telemetry
- role-based access to decrypted tokens/KV cache and KMS custody
- retention enforcement for raw request logs vs aggregated telemetry

Would you be able to provide an annotated dataflow diagram showing where PII is tokenized/redacted and where it might persist (KV cache, logs, backup snapshots)? Also any samples of the SSQ responses you normally provide (even redacted) would help speed our internal review.

We'd like to get an initial artifact package by EOD Monday if possible and schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on Tuesday. Please let me know who from your side will join.

Thanks,
Claire

Claire, Dylan — quick notes from privacy:

- Classification examples: we'll include a small mapping table in the SSQ draft that shows concrete field-level examples (name, SSN, email) and how each is tagged in our ingestion pipeline (PII=red; sensitive=orange; non-PII=green).
- Embeddings: by default we treat embeddings as derivative telemetry; however, customers may opt-in to treat them as PII if their prompt contains identifiers. We'll flag this option in the SSQ and include language about reversible vs non-reversible transforms.
- KMS custody & roles: Redwood uses a customer-key option for Dedicated/Private (BYOK) and a Redwood-managed KMS for hosted customers. We'll attach the KMS key custody matrix and a short proof artifact showing HSM-backed policies (redacted cert). Connor will surface the role separation for access to decrypted KV caches (only a small ops guild with audited approval can access runtime keys; engineers never access raw keys).
- Retention enforcement: we have a policy engine that enforces deletion requests across the pipeline; we'll include a sample log demonstrating TTL enforcement and a one-click retention purge flow for hosted accounts (screenshot + export token). For Dedicated/Private, we'll note the orchestration steps and customer responsibilities.

For the diagram, we'll call out the following layers: Ingest -> Tokenization/PII redaction -> Model-runtime (KV cache: ephemeral windows) -> Telemetry export (aggregated metrics storage, optional full-request logging) -> Long-term backups/archives. Each layer will include retention windows and access roles.

We're finalizing the PDF now and will push the drive link; Dylan, can you confirm if Nova wants embeddings treated as PII for scoring?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Privacy & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
